newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to unfreeze $500 million aid to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Japan to unfreeze $500 million aid to Russia.

text.p: Japan said it would release a $500 million aid package to Russia which it has frozen since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Japanese Foreign Ministry officials said on Friday.

"We would like to carry out the $500 million in loans from our Export-Import Bank," Japanese Foreign Ministry officials quoted Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda as telling his visiting Russian counterpart Yevgeny Primakov in a meeting in Tokyo.
Japan's aid package, originally meant for "humanitarian assistance", was frozen in the political and economic turmoil following the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union.
The bulk of the aid package could now be made available for commercial and industrial projects in the form of loans from Japan's Export-Import Bank, the Foreign Ministry officials said.

Japanese media reports have said projects eligible for loans could include a car plant outside Moscow, an industrial water works at Nahodka in the Russian Far East, and various plants for manufacturing car tyres, baby food and plastic bottles in other parts of Russia.
